Question: A \(25\) foot ladder is placed against a vertical wall of a building. The foot of the ladder is \(7\) feet from the base of the building. If the top of the ladder slips \(4\) feet, then the foot of the ladder will slide:
Solution:
The ladder is the hypotenuse of the right triangle formed with the wall and ground. Its length stays \(25\) feet, so the Pythagorean theorem determines the other lengths in each position.

Initially, the height of the top is
\[
\sqrt{25^2-7^2}=\sqrt{576}=24\text{ feet}.
\]
After slipping \(4\) feet down the wall, the top is \(24-4=20\) feet high. The foot is then
\[
\sqrt{25^2-20^2}=\sqrt{225}=15\text{ feet}
\]
from the wall. We take positive square roots because these are lengths. The foot has moved from \(7\) feet to \(15\) feet from the wall, so it slides \(15-7=8\) feet, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
